items.title: Vince Giordano interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 11, 2007
items.q: And I wrote him a letter and I said I’d love to study with you. And he said fine.

ctx.x: Yeah. Tell me about the Schillinger Method with Bill Challis.

With Bill Challis, yeah. Well joining the union, I got the union directory. And I had been reading this book called “Jazz: the New York Scene” by Charters and Kunstadt. I love that book and it’s a wonderful book. And they mention Bill Challis a few times and I just happened to be flipping in the arranger section and I see William Challis in Massapequa, Long Island. I’m in Smithtown. And I wrote him a letter and I said I’d love to study with you. And he said fine. And my dad, again, takes me out there, because I’m…
left, it had passed these fellows by. You know they just were looking for a gig and hoping to write a song, and that’s a long winded story about the Schillinger Method.

items.title: 68191_William (Bill) H. Challis Oral History Interview
items.q: Vince Giordano, I think, gave it to me.

ctx.x: For Victor. I think it came out. At least I got it on tape up there. They guy -- had to get it from some guy. Vince Giordano, I think, gave it to me.
Well, let's see that didn't last too long because he went in the Army -- he went in the Navy.
